trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court Dewas, Camp Court Barwani, District Barwani in H.M.A. Case No. 21-A/2016
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized in 2004. The respondent/wife started misbehaving and raised doubts about the petitioner's character. The parties have a son named Prince. The petitioner filed a suit for divorce which was later withdrawn, but the respondent/wife continued to misbehave.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty can be physical as well as mental.
legal_principles.held: If it is physical, it is a question of fact and degree. If it is mental, the enquiry must begin as to the nature of the cruel treatment and then as to the impact of such treatment on the mind of the spouse.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh Vs. Jaya Ghosh, (2007)4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: Intention is not a necessary element in cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The absence of intention should not make any difference in the case, if by ordinary sense in human affairs, the act complained of could otherwise be regarded as cruelty.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh Vs. Jaya Ghosh, (2007)4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh Vs. Jaya Ghosh, (2007)4 SCC 511

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment of the trial court is set aside. The parties are directed to live separately.
